apps.name: AiLagoon
apps.shortDescription: AI model hub — aggregate Ollama, ChatGPT, OpenRouter; pin inference transcripts.
apps.description:
# AiLagoon

The AI model hub pearl for Melusina. Register multiple LLM providers,
manage per-model connections, and expose AI capabilities to other
pearls via Grapple — all behind a single Sandstorm HTTP-out permission
to the ai-lagoon sidecar.

## Providers

- **Ollama** — local or remote Ollama server, any model it can host
- **ChatGPT** — OpenAI-compatible API (GPT-4o, 4.1, o1, o3, 4.5, 4.6)
- **OpenRouter** — 100+ models from Anthropic, Google, Meta, Mistral,
  DeepSeek, and more through a single proxy

## Grapple capabilities published by this pearl

Other pearls can request AI from AiLagoon via Grapple:

- `ai-text` — generic text / chat completion
- `ai-vision` — image understanding and OCR
- `ai-generic` — consumer picks a model in the Grapple UI at grant time
- Direct per-model — scoped to one provider + model, useful when a
  consumer wants a specific capability class (e.g. reasoning)

## How HTTP-out works

All providers route through `https://ailagoon.sidecar.host`; the
sidecar's path prefix (`/{provider}/{apiKey}/...`) demultiplexes per
provider. At pearl startup AiLagoon asks Sandstorm for a single
HTTP-out permission to that host — the shell renders the
address-selector popup (not the pearl picker), and the operator grants
or denies the host once. Connections persist across pearl restarts via
`SandstormApi.save()` / `restore()`.

## Playground

A built-in chat playground lets you test any connected model without
leaving the pearl — useful for validating credentials, checking
capabilities, or prototyping prompts before calling them from another
pearl via Grapple. Every assistant reply renders a **provenance card**
underneath the bubble: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, request-ID (cross-
referenceable in `/audit`), provider+connection name, and a
sealed/cleartext pill so compliance officers can attribute and time-
stamp every output without leaving the chat.

## Transcript anchoring — roadmap, not shipped

AiLagoon does **not** currently anchor inference transcripts on-chain.
Earlier catalog copy described "Solana-pinned inference transcripts"
as a shipped feature; that was overclaim. As of v0.7.11 the only
on-chain artifact AiLagoon participates in is the **publish-side**
ReleaseEntry that signs this SPK manifest itself (program
`7anRCW8UAFwdSAAxkrK7TmptukNKY74nZrNPfRKzzWLb`, PDA in the catalog
`attest` block). Per-conversation transcript pinning to the user's
Squads-controlled wallet is on the v0.8 roadmap; until then,
transcripts live append-only in the pearl's encrypted SQLite store
and surface in the audit log as metadata only (no prompt/response
content retained, by design — see `pkg/audit/logger.go`).

apps.description:
BLOOM Identity is a self-hosted KYC (Know Your Customer) identity verification platform for Sandstorm. It lets you run compliant identity checks entirely on your own server — no third-party data processors, no cloud dependencies.

## How It Works

An administrator creates a **Station** grain, configures the verification workflow, and shares a link. Recipients open the link and complete the verification steps in their own **Identity** grain. Results flow back to the Station for review.

### For Administrators

- Create verification workflows with configurable steps
- Share invite links to respondents — no account needed on their end
- Review submitted cases from the Station dashboard
- AI-assisted document and identity analysis (optional, via local Ollama or configured endpoint)
- Case notes, status tracking, and audit logs

### For Respondents

The verification flow guides users through each step:

1. **Terms & Conditions** — Accept the verification terms
2. **Contact Verification** — Email and phone OTP confirmation
3. **Document Upload** — Government ID, passport, or other identity documents
4. **Facial Verification** — Live selfie capture with liveness detection
5. **Personal Details** — Identity form with occupation, source of funds, etc.
6. **Review & Submit** — Confirm all information before submission

Each step is completed in-browser with no app installation required.

## Key Features

- **Privacy-First** — All data stays on your Sandstorm server. Documents, photos, and personal data never leave your infrastructure.
- **Two-Grain Architecture** — Station (admin) and Identity (respondent) grains communicate via Sandstorm's capability system, enforcing strict access control.
- **AI-Powered Analysis** — Optional integration with local LLMs for document OCR, face matching, and risk scoring.
- **Workflow Engine** — YAML-defined verification workflows with conditional steps, configurable per use case.
- **Multi-Language** — Internationalized interface supporting multiple languages.
- **Audit Trail** — Complete journal of all actions for compliance reporting.
- **Responsive Design** — Works on desktop and mobile browsers.

apps.description:
BotMother is a Telegram bot manager with message routing and chatroom support, running on Melusina. Each bot configuration lives in its own Pearl — a sealed, per-document container with its own database, message history, and permissions.

## Why BotMother

- **Pinned chatroom snapshots** — cryptographically anchor any chatroom snapshot to your Solana wallet; snapshots are tamper-evident, citable across Pearls via Grapple, and verifiable independent of the operator
- **Per-bot Pearl isolation** — each bot runs in its own sealed container with separate storage, config, and message logs; no bot Pearl can see another unless you explicitly connect via Grapple
- **Wallet-rooted bot identity** — bot tokens and credentials stored locally; bot ownership linked to Solana wallet; non-repudiable access logs

## Features

- **Message Routing** — define rules to route incoming messages by command, keyword, or sender
- **Chatroom Support** — manage group conversations and route messages between channels
- **Grapple Connections** — link BotMother Pearls to other app Pearls — trigger actions in Bureau spreadsheets, pipe notifications into Mermail, or log events to MiniGit
- **Webhook Integration** — receive and process Telegram webhook events in real-time
- **Privacy-First** — all messages stay on your server; no third-party bot hosting; no message logging by others
- **Offline Queuing** — messages received while offline are queued and processed when the bot reconnects

## Setup

1. Create a bot via BotFather on Telegram
2. Copy the bot token
3. Create a new BotMother Pearl and paste the token
4. Define your routing rules
5. Your bot is live — routing messages through your own server

## Security Model

- Viewer — see bot status and message logs
- Editor — configure routing rules, manage chatrooms
- Admin — manage bot tokens, permissions, and Grapple connections

Every message, every routing rule, every bot token stays inside the Pearl. Server-side permission enforcement — no client-side trust.

## Status

*Production.* Free to install and use on your own server. No subscription, no per-message fees, no limits.

apps.description:
cca.sh Client is the client-facing mode of cca.sh — the MSB/PSP/VASP operator console. As a client you can view balances, submit transactions for approval, and reconcile statements against your organisation's books.

## Why cca.sh Client

- **Wallet-rooted transaction receipts** — cryptographically anchor any transaction receipt to your Solana wallet; receipts are tamper-evident, citable across Pearls via Grapple, and usable as legal proof of settlement
- **Scoped to your seat** — see only what your organisation grants; read + write permissions limited to your role; no cross-client visibility
- **Non-repudiation by design** — every action you take is signed with your Solana key; the audit log proves you requested it, when you requested it, and what you requested

## Features

- **View Balances** — see your account balance and transaction history
- **Submit Transactions** — request debits, transfers, or settlements; routes through the Admin approval gate
- **Reconciliation** — compare transactions against your books; download statements
- **Solana-signed Actions** — every action non-repudiable; no "I didn't request that" plausible deniability
- **No Stored Payment Instruments** — contacts are identity-only, not stored cards
- **Privacy-first** — your transaction history lives on the operator's pearl, not a vendor cloud

## Sibling Apps

- **cca.sh Admin** — full operator console (approval and sign authority)
- **cca.sh Org Member** — team collaboration (draft transactions, shared resources)

## Status

*Pre-release.* The pearl installs today as a Coming Soon stub; the live client UI lands in v0.2.

- **Audit log read-through** — trace any entry back to the signer; see the chain of decision
- **Role-separated from Admin** — no sign authority; confined to draft and propose; no escalation without approval
- **Solana-signed actions** — every draft signed with your key; non-repudiable; audit-ready

apps.description:
cca.sh Wholesale is the institutional pearl of the cca.sh constellation. It owns the four correspondent relationships — SWIFT, SEPA, crypto-custodian, crypto-exchange — at the Fineract / sidecar boundary, and grants per-sub-account capabilities to whitelabel-partner operator Pearls (the popaye / cca.sh-Admin family) over Grapple. End-clients never see this pearl directly; their operator sees it as a Grapple-grant of "settle this envelope to that correspondent at this rate".

## Why cca.sh Wholesale

- **Pinned settlement envelopes** — every settlement request is signed at draft time, pinned to the operator's Solana wallet at approval time, and recorded as an immutable, citable artifact. Disputes between wholesale and a whitelabel partner are resolved against the signed envelope, not a database row that either side could mutate
- **Per-correspondent Grapple capability scoping** — a whitelabel partner's operator pearl claims a sub-account capability scoped to one correspondent + one rate sheet. They cannot see other partners' correspondents; they cannot escalate to the wholesale-admin role; they cannot enumerate the full correspondent topology. Capability surface is enforced at the Cap'n Proto boundary, not at a SaaS endpoint
- **Operator-accountability through wallet signatures** — every wholesale-admin action (correspondent CRUD, rate-sheet edit, sub-account grant) is non-repudiable; the wholesale operator's Solana wallet signs the change. The audit log is provably theirs, not a vendor-database table they can claim was tampered with

## Topology

```
G-ccash Wholesale (this pearl) ─── grants sub-account caps ──▶ G-organization (whitelabel partner)
     │                                                                   │
     ▼                                                                   ▼
finreact-sidecar                                                  G-popaye (operator console)
     │                                                                   │
     ▼                                                                   drafts sends
Fineract GL                                                       emits envelopes
```

## Status

*Pre-release v0.2.0.* The institutional correspondent surface and sub-account grant flow are scaffolded; first end-to-end SWIFT settlement against the live finreact-sidecar lands in v0.3.

- It is not a registered agent. Montana law requires a physical Montana street address; instaco helps you draft the engagement letter, then hands off to your agent
- It is not legal advice. The operating agreement template was reviewed by counsel, but your specific cell structure is yours

## Why Montana Series LLCs

Montana is one of the few US states with a clean series LLC statute, no public member registry, and a Solana-friendly attorney bench. The form-and-fee structure is favorable for asset-protection use cases that need many cells and few annual filings.

Open-source MIT. Production-ready for new entity formation; the K-1 prep module is in active testing for tax year 2026.

# InstaDAO

Deploy and manage a Solana DAO from a single Sandstorm grain. Wizard-driven entity + governance + treasury + cap-table setup, with optional utility-token and holder-voting modules. **Nothing is hardcoded** — each grain stands up its own DAO with its own programs, mint, signers, and parameters.

## What it does

- **10-step Onboarding Wizard** — entity setup, module selection, directors + officers, founders cap-table, OA drafting, deploy quote, on-chain deploy, init-state finalize.
- **DAO Dashboard** — cap-table, governance, treasury, activity for the deployed DAO. Driven by the DAO's own on-chain state — not by any baked-in mint or program.
- **Optional Utility Token** — mint, freeze, burn, standing-offer (USDC + SOL routes) for the DAO's own token, parameterized at deploy time.
- **Optional Holder Voting** — token-weighted proposals with a binding sha256 commitment to question text.
- **Squads-Gated Admin** — every privileged action is a multisig proposal; the grain author can't move the DAO without quorum.
- **Telegram Bot** — optional out-of-band notifications via a Grapple-bound HTTP-out capability.

## Why this design

Sandstorm gives every grain its own root-owned ext4 sandbox + revocable capabilities. We use those to keep the DAO operator's keypairs encrypted at rest, route every Solana RPC through the Melusina shell's `HackSessionContext.solanaRpc` (no outbound HTTP from the grain), and let the operator share read-only or proposal-author roles per Sandstorm's permission grid.

## Upgrading from MLSNA Admin v3.0.x

Existing MLSNA grains auto-upgrade in place — same appId, new versionNumber (51 > 50). Per-tenant config at `/var/melusina/mlsna-admin.env` is still honored; rename to `instadao.env` on the next deploy.

apps.description:
# OpenClaw

A personal AI assistant pearl for Melusina.

OpenClaw is one **Sandstorm pearl**, two processes:

- a **Go capability sidecar** (`openclaw-bridge`) that owns the pearl's
  Cap'n Proto control socket, handles Grapple grants, and exposes a
  loopback HTTP API to the runtime;
- a **Node.js runtime** (the OpenClaw agent) that serves the chat UI,
  runs the inference loop through your AiLagoon pearl, and discovers
  tools from any other Melusina pearl you connect over Grapple.

The two processes are bundled in a single SPK and started together by
`launcher.sh`. There is no `bridgeConfig` — permissions and roles are
defined programmatically in the bridge's `GetViewInfo()`, the same way
AiLagoon, AITX, and BLOOM_FINAL do it.

## Setup

1. Install the SPK on your Melusina instance.
2. Open the **New OpenClaw assistant** action.
3. Use Grapple to grant the new pearl access to an **AiLagoon** pearl
   so the agent can think.
4. Use Grapple to connect any other Melusina grains you want OpenClaw
   to read or act on (Bureau spreadsheets and documents, AITX
   Procedures stations, Mermail mailboxes, Vintage desktops, anything
   that implements the `GrainContext` Cap'n Proto interface).
5. Chat with the assistant to configure monitors, schedules, and
   behaviour. Configuration is conversational and incremental — there
   is no global YAML to author.

## Features

- **Native Melusina pearl** — raw Cap'n Proto, programmatic ViewInfo,
  Grapple-driven capability discovery, persistent state in `/var`.
- **AiLagoon-routed inference** — every LLM call goes through your own
  AiLagoon grain. OpenClaw never holds API keys directly.
- **Per-pearl permission scoping** — each connected pearl decides what
  the agent can see and do, based on the scope of the Grapple grant.
  OpenClaw never interprets app permission tables itself.
- **Wallet-signed critical actions** — operations marked
  `walletSignature` or `threshold` in a pearl's `describe()` must be
  approved by the user's connected Solana wallet via the Melusina
  shell's `requestChainSign()` flow.
- **Two pearl types** — `assistant` (full runtime) and `dev-bridge`
  (sidecar with the demo pearl registered, for testing).

See `MELUSINA_OPENCLAW_INTEGRATION_FINAL.md` in the OpenClaw repository
for the full architecture document and `capnp/graincontext.capnp` for
the universal Cap'n Proto interface every Melusina app implements to
become legible to OpenClaw.

apps.description:
MiniGit provides lightweight, private Git hosting inside a Melusina pearl. Clone, push, browse commits, diffs, and manage branches — all from your browser, entirely on your server.

## Why MiniGit

- **Per-pearl isolation** — each pearl is one sealed repository; separate storage, separate permissions; no cross-pearl leakage; a vulnerability in one pearl cannot reach another
- **Melusina-native access control** — clone, fetch and push are gated by the same share-link permissions (viewer / editor / admin) as the web UI; no separate accounts
- **No third-party CDN/Git gateway** — all repositories hosted locally; no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket; no vendor lock-in; export anytime

## Features

- **One repo per pearl** — the pearl IS the repository; share the pearl to share the repo.
- **Push and pull over HTTPS** — clone URL provided automatically
- **Browse files, commits, and diffs** — in the web UI
- **Share read-only or read/write access** — via standard Melusina sharing
- **No external database** — go-git in-process; the bare repo on disk plus tiny JSON sidecars under the pearl's data dir; zero external services.
- **Fully offline-capable** — no CDN or external calls
- **Role-based access** — viewer, editor, admin

## AI-callable Skills

The pearl exposes a Melusina `GrainContext` capability — its "Skills" — so a compatible AI agent can browse files, read commits, write commits, manage branches, and apply patches through a declarative operations table, called via `describe` / `invoke` over capnp. The operations a caller sees are filtered by the same share-link permission bitset as the human UI: view-only callers never see write operations.

## Status

**Stable (0.2.4)** — full Git hosting (clone / fetch / push over HTTPS), web browsing of trees, blobs, commits and diffs, a lightweight issue + pull-request tracker, and an AI-callable operations surface — all available now.

apps.description:
# TeleScreen Sidecar Configurator

This Sandstorm pearl is the operator-facing configuration UI for the
**TeleScreen sidecar**. It lets you set every knob the
sidecar exposes — secrets, platform toggles, AiLagoon routing, crawl
parameters, storage paths, search providers, product context — entirely
through the browser, with no SSH-into-container required.

The pearl stores its configuration inside its own Sandstorm sandbox
(`/var`) and pushes the merged config to the live sidecar via an
authenticated HTTP-out capability claimed once through the Grapple.
Secrets never touch the sidecar's disk: the sidecar holds them in
process memory, where they are flushed on restart.

This is an admin-only grain. Non-admin users see a read-only landing
page explaining that they need the `admin` permission.

Scope lock: this app is configuration-only and advertises no Cap'n Proto
capabilities. The separate TeleScreen Hub app owns team screening history,
Vintage/AiLagoon/sidecar claims, and the consumer-facing screening service.

apps.description:
Vintage Remote Desktop gives every Melusina operator a disposable, full Linux desktop rendered in the browser. Pearls start in sandbox mode — every change is ephemeral and wiped when the pearl closes. Click Save to upgrade the pearl to a persistent, Solana-backed workspace.

## Why Vintage

- **Pinned session snapshots** — cryptographically anchor any desktop session to your Solana wallet; snapshots are tamper-evident, citable across Pearls via Grapple, and recoverable if the session crashes
- **Ephemeral-first sandbox** — by default, everything is temporary; persistence is an explicit choice, not a default; ideal for one-off work that shouldn't pollute your environment
- **Wallet-rooted persistent state** — when you click Save, session state is anchored to your Solana wallet; ownership and restoration tied to your key; no operator backdoor

## Ideal For

- One-off tooling that you don't want polluting your main environment
- Demo environments that reset cleanly
- Remote-ops consoles where persistence should be an explicit choice, not a default
- Isolated testing and experimentation

## Features

- **Full Linux desktop** — apt, gcc, git, Python, Node, Docker, and standard utilities
- **Browser-based** — no VNC client, no RDP software; open in any browser
- **File transfer** — drag-drop files into the desktop; export files back out
- **Clipboard sync** — paste between your computer and the remote desktop
- **Audio** — WebRTC audio support for VoIP and media playback
- **Offline-capable** — all assets bundled; no external calls

## Status

*Shipped v1.0.0.* Browser-based Linux desktop with ephemeral sandbox default, Solana-pinned session snapshots, full-featured toolchain.
